subject: Clarify: UK IDTA vs. TIA sequencing and subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Bella Roy <bella.roy@healthnova.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@healthnova.com
Date: 2026-06-04T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: Initial: TIA scope and UK IDTA question

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. We've started scoping the TIA/DTIA for our pilot and legal has two asks before we proceed to signatures:

1) Can Redwood execute the UK IDTA (or the UK Addendum) as counterparty, or do we need a separate signature path for subprocessors?
2) We need a short mapping that shows where KV cache, logging, and telemetry are processed (region by service). Can you provide a redwood-subprocessors-latest.csv and a brief note on whether any of those subprocessors are outside the UK/EU and rely on SCCs?

Attaching proposed TIA scope (HealthNova_TIA_scope.xlsx). If you can't provide a UK IDTA signature, what reasonable fallback language do you accept in the DPA to address UK routing?

Goal: get a high-level yes/no on signing plus the CSV and a one-paragraph on routing before Friday so our procurement team can prepare the redline.

Thanks,
Bella Roy
Senior Counsel, HealthNova
bella.roy@healthnova.com

Attachment: HealthNova_TIA_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet – columns: service, data types, region expectation)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Bella Roy <bella.roy@healthnova.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-04T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Initial: TIA scope and UK IDTA question

Hi Bella — thanks for the note and the scope file. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, Redwood can execute the UK IDTA/UK Addendum as counterparty for hosted and dedicated deployments. For Private (customer-managed VPC/on-prem) we typically ask customers to sign both the DPA and the UK addendum because of local control of keys/network.

- I'll attach the latest redwood-subprocessors-latest.csv. Short summary: telemetry/observability pipelines (aggregate traces, metrics) are processed in EU regions; KV cache lives on dedicated GPU nodes that may be allocated in us-east or eu-west depending on routing policy. Where data crosses outside the EU/UK we rely on SCCs+TIA model and maintain records in our transfer log.

I've looped in Markus (legal) to confirm contract language and Marissa from procurement for Docs/DocuSign cadence. We'll follow up with the CSV and a one-paragraph fallback for the DPA by EOD tomorrow.

—Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-subprocessors-latest.csv (stub)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Bella Roy <bella.roy@healthnova.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-05T09:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Initial: TIA scope and UK IDTA question

Hi Bella — a couple of points from legal side:

1) We can countersign the standard UK IDTA / UK Addendum for hosted and dedicated. For Private deployments where the customer controls network and HSM, we ask for a mutual onshore processing rider (short paragraph) instead of a unilateral addendum. I can share redline language if that helps.

2) Regarding subprocessors: Redwood's DPA includes flow-down obligations to subprocessors. We do not require separate signature from every subprocessor — evidence is provided as attestations (SOC2 + written flow-down confirmation) and we maintain a subprocessor register that we can export as CSV.

Proposed fallback DPA paragraph (draft):
"Where Customer lawfully requires data processors to be located in the UK, Redwood will document routing policy and offer onshore-processing fallback as an operational control where feasible. In such cases Redwood will provide a routing attestation and a time-bounded implementation plan agreed with Customer."

If HealthNova wants a guarantee that specific services will only run in the UK, that would be scoped as a residency commitment and priced as a reserved capacity add-on.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Bella Roy <bella.roy@healthnova.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@healthnova.com
Date: 2026-06-05T13:04:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial: TIA scope and UK IDTA question

Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks — that helps. A few clarifying notes from procurement/legal team after reviewing the draft fallback paragraph:

- The HealthNova procurement team is OK with attestations but wants clarity on "routing attestation" — specifically we need the timeframe for implementation and a minimal set of telemetry evidence Redwood will provide to show requests were routed onshore (e.g., sampled logs with timestamps).

- Can you confirm whether the KV cache nodes are covered by the same contractual flow-down? Our security team is concerned about ephemeral KV entries being replicated off-region during autoscaling events.

- Finally, is there an explicit SCCs + TIA packet you provide when transfers rely on SCCs (we expect to upload these to our vendor portal)?

Would appreciate a short packet (one-pager) and the CSV exported. We want to avoid a large redline war.

Best,
Bella

Hi Bella — attaching the CSV and a short packet. See below highlights:

- redwood-subprocessors-latest.csv shows service, region_of_processing, contractual_basis (SCCs/UK_Addendum/Onshore), evidence_bucket_link.
- KV cache: default behavior is in-region; autoscale can pull nodes in compatible regions. For guaranteed residency we offer Dedicated/Reserved capacity with an onshore KV shard option. For hosted we provide sampling logs and a monthly routing attestation.
- SCCs + TIA packet: we have a TIA packet PDF (DocuSign-ready) and an exportable SCC evidence bundle (SCC_templates.zip) — I'll share DocuSign links via Marissa if you want signature flow.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-latest.csv; TIA_packet_onepager.pdf; SCC_templates.zip (stubs).

If HealthNova can accept the attestation + implementation plan language, we can add that as a one-sentence addendum and proceed to DocuSign next week. Otherwise, tell us which services you require residency for and we'll scope pricing.

—Kimberly
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — received the CSV and packet, thanks. Procurement reviewed the one-pager and a couple final asks before we move to signature: 

1) Can you add a single sentence to the TIA packet that confirms Redwood will provide sampled, redacted request-routing logs for a 30-day window post-cutover to verify onshore processing (format: CSV rows with request_id, timestamp_utc, destination_region).
2) For the KV cache question: please add language that the KV cache is subject to the same flow-down and that any autoscaling-driven relocation will be included in the sampled routing logs.

If you can confirm both in writing (we can accept a short email confirmation to attach to our portal) we'll prepare an unredlined UK Addendum for signature.

Wanted to move quickly — thanks for the responsiveness.

Best,
Bella
Senior Counsel, HealthNova
